name: Green tea
caffeine: Commonly 20 to 45 mg per 8 oz cup, partly because it is brewed cooler and shorter; the bands overlap with black.

house.ask: Not printed on the menus: ask at lineup whether the bar pours a green tea, which one, bag or loose leaf, how hot the water runs, and the price.

what: Green tea is Camellia sinensis heated early to kill the enzyme that would oxidise it, so it stays green: steamed in Japan, pan fired in China, and that one choice sets the style. Japanese greens taste grassy and marine, Chinese greens nutty and toasted, towards chestnut. It is unoxidised, not raw, and it wants much cooler water than black tea, which is where most bars go wrong.
taste: Light body with real savoury weight: grassy and marine if Japanese, nutty and toasted if Chinese. Sweet when brewed cool, bitter and drying the moment the water is too hot or the steep too long.

steps: Boil fresh water, then let it fall to 160 to 180F (71 to 82C), or set a variable temperature kettle.
Warm the pot and cup with hot water, then tip it out.
Weigh 2 to 3 g of leaf per 6 to 8 oz of water.
Pour the cooled water over the leaf; the more shaded the leaf, the cooler you go.
Steep 1 to 2 minutes, then pour off every drop so the leaf stops working.
Re-steep two or three times: the second short, the third stretched longer.
make.ratio: 2 to 3 g of leaf per 6 to 8 oz of water
make.dose: 2 to 3 g loose leaf, weighed, or one bag
make.temp: 160 to 180F (71 to 82C); cooler for shaded leaf
make.time: 1 to 2 minutes; re-steeps two or three times
make.cup: Small pot or kyusu into a small cup, 4 to 6 oz

serve: Warm the pot, then let the water cool before it meets the leaf. Send a small pot and a small cup, no milk and no lemon, with a dish for the basket and the time said aloud. Pour off completely and offer more hot water for a second steep. It sits well after sushi or anything fried.
story: The guest who says they hate green tea has usually been served it from a boiling kettle. A full boil pulls catechins and caffeine fast and the bitterness swamps the cup, while the sweet, savoury amino acids come out readily in cooler water. Heat is also what keeps it green: the kill-green step, shaqing in China, done by steam in Japan. Green tea travels, too: Morocco's mint tea is brewed on rolled Chinese gunpowder green, rinsed first, with fresh spearmint and plenty of sugar.
guest: Green tea brews cooler and shorter than black, so it stays sweet and grassy rather than bitter, and the same leaf will give a second pot.
watch: Boiling water does not burn the leaf; it extracts too fast and turns the cup bitter. Let it fall to 160 to 180F (71 to 82C).
A Green Tea ordered at the bar may mean the shot: Irish whiskey, peach schnapps, lemon, syrup and a splash of lemon-lime soda, with no tea in it.
Green fades fastest in the tin and tastes tired inside a year; keep it airtight, dark and away from coffee.

recall.prompt: How is a pot of green tea made?
recall.answer: Water boiled then cooled to 160 to 180F (71 to 82C), 2 to 3 g of leaf per 6 to 8 oz in a warmed small pot, steeped 1 to 2 minutes and poured off completely. Grassy or nutty, sweet, and good for two or three steeps.

quiz.q: Why does green tea brewed at a full boil taste bitter?
options: Catechins and caffeine extract too fast
The amino acids turn bitter in heat
quiz.explain: Heat pulls the bitter, drying catechins and caffeine quickest, while the sweet amino acids come out even in cool water. The cooler steep changes the balance; it is not a weaker cup.

quiz.q: How does most Japanese green tea stop oxidation, compared with most Chinese green tea?
options: Pan fired in place of steaming
Steamed in place of pan firing
quiz.explain: Japan steams nearly all its green tea, which keeps a marine edge; China mostly pan fires, which browns the leaf towards toasted chestnut. That is processing, not latitude.

quiz.q: A guest at the bar orders a Green Tea shot. What goes in it?
options: Irish whiskey, peach schnapps, lemon, syrup, soda
Vodka, peach schnapps, lemon, simple syrup, soda
Matcha liqueur, Irish whiskey, lemon, honey, soda
Green Chartreuse, gin, lime juice, syrup, soda
quiz.explain: The shooter is named for its colour and holds no tea: Irish whiskey, peach schnapps, lemon and syrup, with a splash of lemon-lime soda. Vodka in place of the whiskey makes a White Tea.
